sentences.text:
This is the first application seeking for suspension of sentence and grant of b ail filed on behalf of accused-appellant Lakesh Baghele, who has been convicted under Sections 363, 366-A, 342 and 506 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years, R.I. for 7 years, R.I. for 1 year and R.I. for 1 year and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/-,
Rs.1,000/-, Rs.500/- and Rs.500/- and further convicted under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC merged) and sentenced to undergo life imprisonment and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/-
with default stipulations as mentioned in the impugned judgment dated 04.03.2023 passed by the Special Judge (POCSO Act) District Balaghat in S.C. No.11 of 2022.
3.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: According to the prosecution case, on 01.01.2022, at about 5.30 P.M. the appellant came to the house of the prosecutrix and told the prosecutrix that his grandmother is calling her.
Since the appellant was known to the prosecutrix, she went along with him.
The appellant took her on his motorcycle to Murumtola at her Aunt's residence and on false pretext of marriage, committed rape on her.
On 08.01.2022, a missing report was filed by the complainant.
Thereafter, on 10.01.2022, the prosecutrix was recovered.
Her statement was recorded wherein she alleged against the present appellant for commission of offences as aforementioned.
After trial the appellant was convicted and sentenced as mentioned above.
Questioning the same, the instant appeal has been filed.
4. It is argued that the application of the co-accused - Tarabai has been allowed vide order dated 10.10.2023.
The victim on her own volition has left the house of her parents and accompanied the present appellant.
She has travelled to various places without raising any hue and cry.
She has stayed with the present appellant for almost 9 days.

Document Ex.P/1 which is her initial statement Lakesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89290986/
1 which was recorded by the authorities in presence of the family members does not show commission of offence by the present appellant.

entities.text: Lakesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Rather, subsequently her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and thereafter before this court she has levied allegations against the present appellant regarding commission of offence.
There is no explanation by the prosecution to disbelieve her initial statement.

The investigating officer has admitted in his statement that at the time of recording of initial statement the family members of the victim were present therefore, it cannot be said that under what circumstances she has resiled from her earlier statement.
The applicant is in custody for about 1 year 2 months.
He is ready to abide by all terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court while considering his application.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of suspension of sentence and bail.

5. Per contra, State counsel has vehemently opposed the application stating that the witness has supported the case of the prosecution as is reflected from statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
and thereafter before the trial court.
But, he could not dispute that in her statement recorded as PW-1 there is no allegation being levied against the present appellant.
The fact that the co- accused has already been enlarged on bail could not be disputed by the prosecution.
6. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case but without commenting upon the merits, we deem it just and necessary to enlarge the appellant on bail.
Consequently, I.A. No.26980 of 2023 is allowed.

7. Appellant - Lakesh Baghele is directed to be enlarged on bail, if he is not required in any other offence, subject to he depositing the fine amounts and on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the concerned Court/CJM on 03.04.2024 and thereafter on such other subsequent dates as may be fixed in that behalf.

(RAVI MALIMATH) (VI  CHIEF JUSTICE   LR Lakesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89290986/
